antidotes.source: Bhartrihari Niti 71; Nahusha; Bali to Indra
antidotes.why: Vinaya teaches that fruit-laden trees bow and fortune sat with thousands before you.
Seeing what else made the success.

verses.m: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
verses.sa: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥

verses.m: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
verses.sa: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥

refs: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Narada to Shuka, quoting Sanatkumara)
chains.summary: You should guard your discipline from anger, your fortune from envy, your learning from pride and slight, and yourself from heedlessness.
chains.title: Guard each thing from its thief

verses.m: Always guard your discipline from anger and your good fortune from envy; guard your learning from both pride and insult, and guard yourself from carelessness.
verses.sa: नित्यं क्रोधात्तपो रक्षेच्छ्रियं रक्षेच्च मत्सरात् / विद्यां मानावमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः

chains.summary: Hope takes away steadiness, envy takes right conduct, anger takes fortune, bad company takes character, desire takes modesty, and pride takes everything.
chains.title: What each one takes from you

verses.m: Age steals beauty, craving steals patience, death takes life, envy takes goodness, anger takes prosperity, bad company takes character, lust takes shame, and pride takes everything.
verses.sa: जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा / मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया / क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्यसेवा / ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः

chains.summary: Pride is the root of the round of sorrows and the giver of every pain. The Lord removes it from those he loves, just as a mother has a child's boil lanced though the child cries.
chains.title: Pride, the root

verses.m: Hear Ram's natural way: he never lets pride stay in his devotee, for pride is the root of the cycle of birth and death, the giver of many pains and of every sorrow.
verses.sa: नहु राम कर सहज सुभाऊ। जन अभिमान न राखहिं काऊ॥ संसृत मूल सूलप्रद नाना। सकल सोक दायक अभिमाना ॥

depicts.m: When I knew a little, I was blind with pride like an elephant in rut, and my mind swelled: 'I know everything.' When, little by little, I learned from the wise, I realised 'I am a fool', and my pride left me like a fever.
depicts.sa: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं गज इव मदान्धः समभवम् तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः । यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतम् तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥
depicts.why: Depicts blind like an elephant in rut.

depicts.m: Prosperity deludes a person, however wise and brave. Anyone living in comfort fails to notice it happening. That is my view.
depicts.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
depicts.sa: सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम् / वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो नावैतीति मतिर्मम
depicts.why: Shows a king who fell through this very blindness and now sees it.

depicts.m: Once I moved through the sky in a celestial chariot, drunk on pride, and gave no thought to anyone else.
depicts.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
depicts.sa: अहं हि दिवि दिव्येन विमानन चरन्पुरा / अभिमानेन मत्तः सन्कंचिन्नान्यमचिन्तयम्
depicts.why: Depicts Nahusha describing his own intoxication with success.

depicts.m: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice': so they say, deluded by ignorance.
depicts.sa: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥

gloss: Intoxication with one's own wealth, learning, birth or power. Nahusha says success blinds even the wise.

heals.m: Trees bow low with fruit; clouds hang low with new rain; the good are not puffed up by prosperity. This is the very nature of those who help others.
heals.sa: भवन्ति नम्रास्तरवः फलोद्गमै- र्नवाम्बुभिर्दूरविलम्बिनो घनाः । अनुद्धताः सत्पुरुषाः समृद्धिभिः स्वभाव एवैष परोपकारिणाम् ॥

heals.m: This royal fortune that you think rests with you: that is false. It has never stayed with anyone. It lived with thousands of Indras greater than you, and has now left me and come to you.
heals.sa: यामेतां प्राप्य जानीषे राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम् / स्थिता मयीति तन्मिथ्या नैषा ह्येकत्र तिष्ठति स्थिता हीन्द्रसहस्रेषु त्वद्विशिष्टतमेष्वियम् / मां च लोला परित्यज्य त्वामगाद्विबुधाधिप
heals.why: Shows success as a visitor, not a possession.

heals.m: Prosperity deludes a person, however wise and brave. Anyone living in comfort fails to notice it happening. That is my view.
heals.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
heals.sa: सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम् / वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो नावैतीति मतिर्मम
heals.why: Names the way success numbs self-awareness.

heals.m: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
heals.sa: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते

heals.m: Alert, deep, steadfast, master of the six waves of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age and death; seeking no honour yet honouring others; capable, friendly, compassionate, wise.
heals.sa: अप्रमत्तो गभीरात्मा धृतिमान् जितषड्गुणः । अमानी मानदः कल्पो मैत्रः कारुणिकः कविः ॥

heals.m: Cut off craving, practise forbearance, give up arrogance, take no delight in wrong, speak the truth, follow the path of the good, serve the wise, honour those worthy of honour, win over even your enemies, show courtesy, guard your good name, be kind to those in pain: this is how the good behave.
heals.sa: तृष्णां छिन्धि भज क्षमां जहि मदं पापे रतिं मा कृथाः सत्यं ब्रूह्यनुयाहि साधुपदवीं सेवस्व विद्वज्जनम् । मान्यान् मानय विद्विषोऽप्यनुनय प्रख्यापय प्रश्रयं कीर्तिं पालय दुःखिते कुरु दयामेतत् सतां चेष्टितम् ॥

heals.m: "All of it was your glory, Lord. None of it was my own greatness."
heals.sa: सो सब तव प्रताप रघुराई। नाथ न कछू मोरि प्रभुताई ॥
heals.why: Shows success not allowed to go to his head.

heals.m: Even a sole master of the fourteen worlds cannot last if he makes enemies of living beings. A person may be an ocean of virtues and clever too, but if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
heals.sa: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
heals.why: Gives lordship of fourteen worlds does not protect one who harms others.

hero.m: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice': so they say, deluded by ignorance.
hero.sa: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥

loci.m: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and against the rules.
loci.sa: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥

modern: Drunk on success, pride of wealth or standing

practices.m: One who watches his own active body as if it were someone else's: how could praise or blame disturb such a large-hearted person?
practices.sa: चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् । संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥
practices.why: Shows being unshaken by praise and blame.

practices.m: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
practices.sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
practices.why: Gives evenness as the very definition of yoga.

practices.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
practices.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows offering even a little as thanks.

practices.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
practices.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
practices.why: Shows speaking openly of help received.

practices.m: Keep a grateful heart and a friendly spirit. Everything grows out of friendship; a friend is the greatest blessing.
practices.sa: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्
practices.why: Names gratitude as the disposition to hold.

practices.m: Never give up what is right out of desire, rage or hatred. Don't be overjoyed by what pleases you, nor burn with distress at what does not.
practices.sa: न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत् / प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्
practices.why: Shows neither over-joy nor fever at events.

practices.m: Whether he wins or fails, the wise person does not keep grieving. He starts on the next task at once and does not hoard his own life.
practices.sa: अलब्ध्वा यदि वा लब्ध्वा नानुशोचति पण्डितः / आनन्तर्यं चारभते न प्राणानां धनायते
practices.why: Shows gain and failure getting the same response.

practices.m: Gathering the threads of attachment to all of these, he twists them into one cord and ties his mind to my feet. Even-minded, wanting nothing, with no elation, grief or fear in his mind: such a good person lives in my heart as wealth lives in a miser's heart. Saints like you are dear to me; I take a body for no other reason.
practices.sa: सब कै ममता ताग बटोरी। मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥ समदरसी इच्छा कछु नाहीं। हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं ॥ अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें। लोभी हृदयँ बसइ धनु जैसें॥ तुम्ह सारिखे संत प्रिय मोरें। धरउँ देह नहिं आन निहोरें ॥
practices.why: Shows seeing alike and wanting nothing.

stories.l: Strength without humility is blind. The one blocking your path may be family.
stories.s: Searching for a flower for Draupadi, mighty Bhima finds an old monkey blocking the path and orders it to move. Told to lift its tail himself, he cannot budge it. The monkey is his elder brother Hanuman, who embraces him and teaches him.

stories.l: Do the work, give away the credit, and ask only to keep loving.
stories.s: Back from Lanka, Hanuman tells Ram how Sita survives: his name guards her day and night. Ram, in tears, asks whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers that the only calamity is forgetting him. Ram says he can never repay Hanuman and cannot even look him in the face; Hanuman falls at his feet and will not get up. Offered anything, he asks only for unwavering devotion, and credits every deed to Ram.

stories.l: The moment you boast of beating a weakness, it has found another way in.
stories.s: Narada conquers desire in meditation and cannot stop telling people about it. Vishnu creates a city and a princess's swayamvara; Narada falls for her and asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu, like a doctor refusing harmful food, gives him a monkey's face instead, and Narada is laughed out of the hall until he sees what his pride has done.
stories.t: Narada's pride and the monkey face

stories.l: Learning without humility misses the main thing.
stories.s: After twelve years of study, Shvetaketu returns home at twenty-four full of himself. His father gently asks whether he learned the one thing that makes everything else understood, and the son admits his teachers never taught it.
